title: Ancient Trees in Spain: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Spain's oldest urban trees are mostly foreigners: ombues, dragon trees and figs that came back on ships. Fifteen cities mapped, 222 trees.
intro: Spain's great native trees are out in the countryside, in the dehesas where holm oaks stand a hundred paces apart over grazing pigs. What grows in its cities came back on ships. The ombu in Seville is from the Argentine pampas, the dragon trees are Canarian, the Moreton Bay figs are Australian and the ahuehuetes are Mexican, and they are here because Seville and Cadiz held the monopoly on trade with the Americas and captains brought seedlings home the way other people bring back souvenirs. The result is that a Spanish city garden is a record of where its ships went. It also explains the ages: most of these trees arrived with the botanical fashion of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, so two hundred years is old here and five hundred is exceptional.
